reelection.rule: Rule: next even-year November for this House term. legislators-current.yaml ends the current term on 2027-01-03. The even-year November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file has no election day, so no day of the month is shown.

posts.text:
It was a privilege to honor the veterans and their families at Brittany Pointe in Lansdale. 

I am in awe of their service which especially at such consequential moments of our nation’s history demanded unparalleled courage, strength, and love of country. 

Our veterans are the https://t.co/GmhJY3OjYy

I am alarmed by the increasing attacks on freedom of the press in Egypt, which recently charged multiple journalists, including Lina Attalah, the editor of independent media outlet Mada Masr, on politically motivated grounds.

I join @RMGregoryMeeks and @HFACDems in calling for Egypt to immediately reverse the closure of Mada Masr, halt its attacks on the free press, and release these wrongfully detained journalists.

https://t.co/wsJSwxQIkK

Last week, Americans made their voices heard — no more chaos, corruption, or cruelty.
  
Families deserve lower costs, quality healthcare, and a government that works for them.
  
It’s time to rebuild, renew, and deliver for the American people. https://t.co/gpapnw6dZW
Our national security must never come second to politicians’ personal interests. https://t.co/4GtZGfCU9B

The best way to honor our veterans is to guarantee all the benefits they have so rightly earned.

Today's passage of the Major Richard Star Act will help ensure that. https://t.co/4GtuCm6npD

As we honor America's veterans today, I was grateful to visit the newly-dedicated Desert Shield and Desert Storm memorial on the National Mall, and to meet some Gulf War veterans from Pennsylvania and Maryland. 
 
I thank Brian, John, Chris, and Carmello, as well as all our nation's veterans, for their selfless service.
Americans voted for affordability and accountability, and I look forward to working alongside our many new members to deliver on just that. https://t.co/fzPKBVFmC3
Americans elected a historic Democratic majority to focus on affordability and accountability. We will. https://t.co/KH4wVkpbSL

Happy Diwali!

May this Festival of Lights bring an abundance of light, happiness, and prosperity. https://t.co/m9sGjOybc7

I'm guided by my faith — including the call to feed the hungry.

In Montgomery County, 85,000 people face hunger. SNAP and Medicaid cuts have deepened the hurt of our most vulnerable. We must do better. 

That's why I was moved to speak with the Montco Anti-Hunger Network, more than 70 food pantries dedicated to feeding our neighbors. Thank you for your truly tireless advocacy.

I am disturbed by reports that businesses in Philadelphia are being targeted for boycotts because they have Jewish owners. 

We are guaranteed the right to peaceful protest and to freedom of speech. It is fundamental to who we are as Americans. That includes the freedom to oppose the war in Gaza, and the actions of the Netanyahu government. 

Yet we must speak clearly when confronted with blatant antisemitism. Targeting businesses simply because they are owned by Jews — and on the eve of Kristallnacht, when Nazis terrorized Jewish families, businesses and synagogues — is unacceptable. 

I believe protesting in this way is harmful and misguided, and I urge the organizers to desist.

posts.text:
It's time to talk about what comes next.
 
Looking forward to our conversation, today at 3:00 PM ET! https://t.co/jbbny8RK7C

It continues to be the greatest and most solemn privilege of my life to serve Berks and Montgomery Counties.

Thank you for entrusting me with another term representing Pennsylvania’s Fourth Congressional District. 

Last night was a resounding rejection of the chaos, corruption, https://t.co/Ram6kfKxb7

Polls are open until 8 PM. 🗳️

Make your voice heard, Pennsylvania! 🇺🇸 https://t.co/B3zP1LbWb1

Our seniors deserve to live comfortably and to age with dignity. 

So, I was glad to secure Community Project Funding for the Montgomery County Housing Authority to make ADA upgrades to their residences.
 
And it was a joy to visit Lee Towers in Conshohocken to see these https://t.co/k0kAzn6zpP

Early in my time in Congress, the late Elijah Cummings shared with me a message of hope.
 
Let's remember we all have a stake in our democracy, and every voice deserves to be heard. https://t.co/X6AghLZw8t

As Election Day nears, have your voting plan in place to make your voice heard! 🗳️

If you are voting via mail ballot, you can return it to a Drop Box.

Locations for Berks and Montgomery Counties can be found here ➡️ https://t.co/mujX4jncim

Government has a role to play in ensuring families can access healthy food.

As our region confronts rising levels of hunger — in large part to SNAP cuts — we must do better for our most vulnerable.

Thanks to FoodTank & WHYY for a conversation on nutrition and federal policy. https://t.co/W6gUpGM85f

Children belong in classrooms and playgrounds, not in for-profit detention centers.
 
Kids have a right to an education in the United States, but this administration will go to extreme lengths to deny it to them. https://t.co/OASqCQFhao

PA leads the nation in measles cases. 5 people have died.
 
Governor Shapiro has taken this threat seriously, RFK Jr. has not.
 
We cannot let this administration’s disregard for science reverse decades of public health progress. https://t.co/JunqzYFXOa

With voting underway across the country, Pennsylvania voters have until 5:00 PM today to request a mail-in ballot.
  
Whether you vote by mail or in-person, make your voice heard. https://t.co/gCiCozioh1

Eight years ago, we witnessed the deadliest antisemitic attack in U.S. history — 11 worshippers killed at the Tree of Life Synagogue.

Our Jewish community — and members of all faiths — deserve the right to worship unafraid. It is core to who we are as Americans.

At a time of rising violent antisemitism, we must all do our part to reject hate.

Today my prayers are with the families still grieving, the Tree of Life community, and the city of Pittsburgh. May their memories be a blessing.

posts.text:
This administration took us into a war they don’t know how to end. 
 
We need real diplomats. https://t.co/fKraSDtwuM

From pioneering vaccine treatments to cutting-edge research on HIV and heart disease, Montco is shaping the future of medicine.
 
Glad to celebrate Merck’s historic $2.8 billion investment right here at home, strengthening our local economy and our commitment to the life sciences!

Today we're celebrating a $10 million federal investment in railroad infrastructure, strengthening connections across Pottstown, Stowe, Greshville, Boyertown, Bechtelsville, and Bally — including at the historic Colebrookdale Railroad!
 
Together, we’re building a stronger, safer, more connected Pennsylvania.

Ukraine is our ally, yet this administration's actions suggest otherwise.
  
We must stand with the people of Ukraine in their fight for sovereignty against Russia’s illegal, brutal invasion. https://t.co/LomxvBIlM1

Congratulations to Glenside’s very own SSG Colin Doyle on being named U.S. Army Special Operations Command Non-Commissioned Officer of the Year at the annual AUSA Conference! 🇺🇸

I am in awe of the grit and sacrifice our servicemembers show each and every day. 

The future of our young servicemembers is bright — our nation more secure — with NCOs like SSG Doyle leading and training our most advanced military units.

https://t.co/MCs1ZRCwt1

Glad to kick off another year of our student taskforce! 📚

Our young people are bright, thoughtful, and curious about the world around them — and what they can contribute to it. I am energized whenever I can learn from their experiences and their spirit. 
 
Thank you to Abington School District and PSEA for hosting.

As the climate crisis worsens, our farmers, chefs, restaurants, and all those who feed us are hit hardest.

Article 1, Section 27 of the PA Constitution guarantees the right to a healthy environment, and it is our responsibility to be stewards.
 
I was fortunate to join Christa Barfield, founder of FarmerJawn, on her beautiful land in Elkins Park; the James Beard Foundation; and culinary leaders for a critical conversation about sustainability, hunger, and the necessary collaboration at every level of agriculture.

Members of Congress should not have to do the work this administration was required — by law — to finish months ago.
 
Survivors of Epstein deserve justice, and Americans deserve the truth. https://t.co/2JvEUXHPfG

I am heartbroken to hear of the death of Philadelphia police officer Shane Seiber in the line of duty today. My thoughts are with his grieving family, as well as the family of another officer who was wounded—I am praying for his recovery. 
  
Our law enforcement officers put their lives on the line to protect us. I will always stand with them and will never forget the risks they take every day for our safety.

Desperate to escape the consequences of his failed Iran war, Trump is preparing to stab Ukraine in the back and buy diesel from Putin.
  
He's helping fund Russia's war machine, while our allies pay the price.
 
Read more, here: https://t.co/YgxhMMZx4o

Please join me for a Town Hall on October 21 in Abington!

RSVP is required. Location details to come ➡️ https://t.co/g5O2cwdKo3

Looking forward to a great discussion! https://t.co/DixDPCFNYL

Three years ago today, Hamas terrorists launched a brutal, barbaric — most inhumane — attack on the people of Israel. Homes, Kibbutzim, and families were burned. Families torn apart. Unspeakable crimes committed against women, children, and seniors. More than 1,200 people were killed and 250 taken hostage, including American citizens.

The cruelty and brutality of this attack demanded universal, international condemnation and American support for our ally and friend Israel.

I have traveled to Israel several times since October 7th, to meet with grieving Israeli families and government leaders. I met twice with Prime Minister Netanyahu, urging him to pursue justice — a just war — not vengeance, to be a partner for peace.

Today, thanks to the tireless advocacy from the families and to American leadership, all the living hostages have been reunited with their loved ones. The dead have been returned to be buried with dignity. Around the world, Jewish people just celebrated their first Rosh Hashanah without any hostages held in Hamas’ custody. But the scars of October 7th run deep and are lasting. The families of those who were killed, and those who were taken, will carry that grief for the rest of their lives. We all will.

Meanwhile, the region remains in turmoil. Millions of Gazans are still displaced and vulnerable, struggling to find the food, water, medicine, and shelter they need to survive. More than 70,000 innocent Palestinian civilians have been killed and thousands more wounded, so many of them children. and Israeli violations of the ceasefire are alarmingly common. In the West Bank, Israeli settlers continue to encroach on Palestinian land, using violence to injure, kill, and drive out Palestinian families, jeopardizing any chance at peace.

We owe it to all those who died, on that day and in the devastating war since, to build a better future. 

My prayer, and my work as a member of Congress, remains focused on supporting these essential pillars of peace: disarming of Hamas, a durable ceasefire to enable the mass distribution of humanitarian aid to the people of Gaza; a safe and secure future for Israel as a democratic home for the Jewish people; self-determination and dignity for the Palestinian people to rebuild their lives and create a democratic, sovereign state of their own; and a commitment by leaders around the world to these principles, that we might truly end the cycle of violence. 

In this work, I am guided by the Jewish teaching of “Tikkun Olam”— the call to repair the world — and by the Scripture which tells us: blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called children of God.

Today, we remember the suffering of October 7th. Tomorrow, we must continue the work, with mercy and moral clarity, each doing our part to make peace.

I am deeply disturbed by the vile antisemitic and anti-Black graffiti spray painted at the Glenside Weldon playground. 

At a park — where children deserve to feel safe and protected. 
 
On the cusp of three years since the horrific attacks against the Jewish community on October 7th, we must always unite against hate and against those who try so hard to divide us.

Today is a Good Day offers resources and support to NICU families across our region —  solace during times of great uncertainty.

It was a privilege to secure Community Project Funding for their team, and I was glad to visit them in Flourtown to hear how those federal dollars expanded their family advocacy in our local hospitals.

Thank you for your big work for our littlest. 💚

The President says we should sit still on AI.
 
Americans and the industry know better.
 
We have the proposals. We have the support across the aisle. We must pass guardrails on AI before it's too late. https://t.co/0qTkYgVI1q

I was thrilled to help open the Schuylkill River Trail’s final portion in Montgomery County — adding to its gorgeous, nearly 70-mile stretch.
 
This project is decades in the making, a dream realized for our communities to bike, walk, run, and take in the beauty of our natural resources.

Thank you to our state and local leaders for making this possible.
Read more, here: https://t.co/aTYCjwc77I

AI deepfakes are stealing our voices, faces, and identities.
 
The technology is moving fast, but the law hasn't caught up.
 
That’s why Congresswoman Salazar and I introduced the NO FAKES Act — to put the power over your voice and likeness back where it belongs — with you.
Read the full story here ➡️ https://t.co/5mVEX15hpG

President Trump gave ICE and CBP billions of your tax dollars. They have used those dollars to terrorize our communities, kill immigrants and Americans, and now to tell you what a great job Trump is doing.
 
This is an abuse of power, and Democrats will hold them accountable.

This administration wants voters to be intimidated because they know they're losing.
  
Don't let the lies and fearmongering win — our elections are free and fair. All voters should feel empowered to use their voice. https://t.co/VlSkw76OSE

The survivors of Jeffrey Epstein deserve justice.
 
While in Dallas, I viewed an exhibit of more than 300 million pages of the Epstein Files. It is a brave and urgent project that aims to uncover the despicable crimes of Epstein and his associates, and to give voice to the women and girls who suffered their abuse.
 
My visit, and the fearless organizers who I met, will stay with me for a long time. We must never stop pursuing justice.

Our veterans represent the very best of us — and I am always eager to learn from their experiences to help guide my work.

Thank you to our Veterans Advisory Panel (and the veterans on my team!) for giving their insights on how we can better support veterans as they establish their civilian lives.

With one in four nurses assaulted at work and many leaving the profession, we must do better for those who give us their best when we are at our worst.
 
Kevin Mahoney, Penn Medicine CEO, and I wrote about how we can better protect our healthcare workers. 

Read our Op-Ed here. ➡️ https://t.co/jnhAiZOWyM
Republicans had their chance to govern, instead they chose to support this administration’s corruption and incompetence. https://t.co/8TscgM3bM5

I was delighted to celebrate 73 years of the United States—Republic of Korea alliance.

Following the staggering loss of American and South Korean troops in the Korean War, the Eisenhower Administration forged the US-ROK Mutual Defense Treaty. President Eisenhower wrote that “the security of an individual nation in the free world depends upon the security of its partners.” 

I was especially grateful to Master Yang, our local VFWs, and our Korean-American community for organizing this event in North Wales — a strong reminder of our duty to uphold that very same commitment to long-lasting peace.
G'mar chatima tovah — wishing a meaningful time of reflection and easy fast to all those observing Yom Kippur. https://t.co/1jF0AdYjOc

As Congress is sent home and votes are cancelled, the Speaker will be remembered for his failure to govern.
 
We can do better. https://t.co/0B0ylwcao9

funding.heading: Disclosed campaign receipts
funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.

town_halls.note: There is no national town-hall dataset. Dates are not estimated.

disclosure_note: Disclosed contributions only; donors behind groups that do not report their own donors are not in this feed.
